title: Law, guidance, standard or rulebook?
brief: A customer asks for ISO 42001, a regulator for EU AI Act evidence and the board for NIST alignment. Decide which framework you adopt first, say what each one is and is not, and decide what you will not claim.

blocks.text: Four kinds of document, often confused

blocks.caption: What each framework is. Dates and statuses checked 2026-10-13.
head: Framework
Kind
Binding or certifiable
Covers
Date and status
rows: Binding in the EU. Not a certificate
Released 2023-01-26. NIST says it is being revised [[r10]]
Twelve GenAI risks with suggested actions
An organization's AI management system (AIMS), Plan-Do-Check-Act
Six goal groups, including human oversight and control
Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security chapters

blocks.md:
A **regulation** says what you must do in a jurisdiction. A **guidance framework** such as the NIST AI RMF gives a shared vocabulary and practices and is voluntary. A **management system standard** such as ISO/IEC 42001 lets an independent body certify that your organization runs an AI management system. An **internal standard** turns principles into engineering requirements.

The common mistake is to mix them. An ISO 42001 certificate covers the organization's management system, not the behaviour of one chatbot, and NIST AI RMF is not a regulation. NIST AI 600-1 names twelve GenAI risks: CBRN information or capabilities, confabulation, dangerous, violent or hateful content, data privacy, environmental impacts, harmful bias and homogenization, human-AI configuration, information integrity, information security, intellectual property, obscene, degrading or abusive content, and value chain and component integration. Prompt injection and data poisoning sit under information security.

blocks.title: Which framework do you adopt first?
blocks.prompt: Set where you sell, whether customers ask for a certificate and how many teams build AI. The first choice changes. Most organizations end up with a combination.

options.name: EU AI Act programme
options.summary: Map duties by role and date and build evidence.

options.name: NIST AI RMF with the GenAI profile
options.summary: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, with twelve GenAI risks.

options.name: Internal standard in the Microsoft style
options.summary: Goals, requirements and a Sensitive Uses review.

options.name: Lightweight checklist
options.summary: The boring option, sized to one product.

eu.why: Binding law for systems on the EU market.

other.why: No legal driver unless you serve EU users.

none.why: A legal duty needs no customer ask.

cert.why: It is not a certificate customers can request.

many.why: A shared programme pays off across systems.

eu.why: Not a legal answer in the EU.

other.why: A common voluntary reference outside the EU.

one.why: Light to apply to one product.

many.why: The Govern function scales across teams.

eu.why: Supports compliance but does not prove it.

global.why: One international standard for every region.

cert.why: Certifiable, which is what procurement asks for.

many.why: A management system pays off across teams.

other.why: Fits when no law drives you.

many.why: Shared goals and a Sensitive Uses review scale across teams.

eu.why: Will not satisfy a legal duty.

many.why: Does not scale to a fleet.

blocks.takeaway: The law decides what you must do, a certificate decides what customers accept, and a voluntary framework decides how you organise the work. Pick the one your strongest driver demands, then borrow from the others.

items.symptom: A sales deck says the chatbot is ISO 42001 certified.
items.cause: The certificate covers the organization's AI management system, not the behaviour of one application.
items.fix: Say the management system is certified and show application evidence: evals, oversight records and incident drills.

items.symptom: NIST AI RMF is cited as a regulation, or without a version.
items.cause: It is voluntary guidance, and NIST says 1.0 is being revised under the White House AI Action Plan.
items.fix: Cite the version, call it voluntary and map its functions to your controls.

items.symptom: The control mapping is complete but no one can show it operating.
items.cause: Controls were listed without records that prove them.
items.fix: Tie every control to evidence: approval logs, review dates, eval results and incident exercises.

items.symptom: A customer asks for EU AI Act evidence and receives an ISO certificate.
items.cause: Law and management system answer different questions.
items.fix: Map duties by role and date. ISO 42001 can support compliance but does not prove it.

items.title: Go deeper: the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard v2

blocks.md: The June 2022 external release has six goal groups: accountability, transparency, fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, and inclusiveness. Accountability includes goal A5, human oversight and control, and a Sensitive Uses review that is repeated at least annually. It is one company's internal rulebook, a useful template, not a certification [[r13]].

items.title: Go deeper: the GPAI Code of Practice

blocks.md: Published on 2025-07-10 and voluntary. The Commission and the AI Board confirmed it as an adequate voluntary compliance tool. The Transparency and Copyright chapters cover Article 53 for all GPAI providers, and the Safety and Security chapter covers Article 55 for models with systemic risk [[r9]].

blocks.title: What interviewers listen for
blocks.md: Say what each framework is before you pick one: law, guidance, certifiable standard or internal rulebook. Then say what you will not claim, for example that ISO 42001 certifies one chatbot or that NIST is binding.

quiz.q: What does an ISO/IEC 42001 certificate show?
options: An audited organization-level AI management system
The chatbot will not produce harmful or inaccurate answers in production
The system meets the EU AI Act high-risk requirements
The system passed the twelve risk tests in NIST AI 600-1
quiz.explain: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies and certifies an AI management system for an organization, run as Plan-Do-Check-Act. It does not certify one application's behaviour, it does not prove EU AI Act compliance and NIST AI 600-1 is a voluntary profile with suggested actions, not a test suite.

quiz.q: Select every true statement about the NIST AI RMF and AI 600-1.
options: AI RMF 1.0 was released on 2023-01-26 and is voluntary.
AI 600-1 is the GenAI profile, released 2024-07-26, with twelve risks.
The four functions are Plan, Do, Check and Act.
NIST states that AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.
The AI RMF is a regulation with fines for non-compliance.
quiz.explain: The RMF is voluntary guidance with the functions Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, the GenAI profile lists twelve risks, and NIST says 1.0 is under revision. Plan-Do-Check-Act is the ISO management system cycle, and the RMF carries no fines.

quiz.q: A 15-person startup ships one chatbot to US customers. No customer asks for a certificate and no binding AI law applies. Which first step fits?
options: Build a full EU AI Act compliance programme
Adopt the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard unchanged
A short checklist mapped to NIST functions
quiz.explain: With one product, no certificate demand and no binding law, a lightweight checklist mapped to the NIST functions is right-sized and can grow later. ISO certification is heavy for one product, the EU programme answers a legal driver you do not have and a large internal standard copied unchanged adds process without a driver.

takeaways: Law, guidance, certifiable standard and internal rulebook answer different questions.
ISO/IEC 42001 certifies an organization's management system, not one chatbot.
NIST AI RMF is voluntary, 1.0 is under revision, and AI 600-1 lists twelve GenAI risks.
Pick the framework your strongest driver demands, then borrow from the others.
Evidence beats mapping: tie every control to a record.
